/-!
# Conjecture 7.49

by V. I. Trofimov

Let $G$ be a finitely generated group, and $N$ a minimal normal subgroup of $G$ which is an
elementary abelian $p$-group. Is it true that either $N$ is finite or the growth function for
the elements of $N$ with respect to a finite generating set of $G$ is bounded below by an
exponential function?

Here the growth function for the elements of $N$ with respect to a finite generating set $S$
of $G$ is $n \mapsto \#\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\}$, where $|x|_S$ is the word length of $x$ in
$G$ with respect to $S$. Whether it is bounded below by an exponential function does not depend
on the choice of $S$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.49» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G] (p : ℕ), p.Prime →
      ∀ N : Subgroup G, Minimal (fun H : Subgroup G => H.Normal ∧ H ≠ ⊥) N →
        IsMulCommutative N → (∀ x ∈ N, x ^ p = 1) →
        Finite N ∨ ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ →
          ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧
            ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (((N : Set G) ∩ CayleyBall S n).ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group, and $N$ a minimal normal subgroup of $G$ which is an
elementary abelian $p$-group. Is it true that either $N$ is finite or the growth function for
the elements of $N$ with respect to a finite generating set of $G$ is bounded below by an
exponential function?

Here $N$ is a minimal normal subgroup of $G$ if it is minimal among the nontrivial normal
subgroups of $G$, and $N$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group ($p$ a prime) if it is abelian and
$x^p = 1$ for all $x \in N$. The growth function for the elements of $N$ with respect to a
finite generating set $S$ of $G$ is $n \mapsto \#\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\}$, where $|x|_S$ is
the word length of $x$ with respect to $S$; the set $\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\}$ is the
intersection of $N$ with the ball of radius $n$ in the Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $S$
(`CayleyBall S n`). It is bounded below by an exponential function if there is a constant
$c > 1$ with $\#\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\} \ge c^n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This
property does not depend on the choice of the finite generating set $S$ of $G$, so it is
required for every finite generating set.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no Prop universally quantified over all finitely generated G, primes p, and minimal normal subgroups N that are elementary abelian p-groups (i.e. N is a nontrivial normal subgroup with no proper nontrivial G-normal subgroup, and an F_p-vector space); the growth function is n ↦ #{x ∈ N : word length of x w.r.t. a finite generating set S of G ≤ n}, and 'bounded below by an exponential' means ∃ c > 1 with f(n) ≥ c^n for all (sufficiently large) n — a property independent of the choice of finite generating set S, so quantifying over every S or some S is equivalent, but the quantifier over S should be made explicit; the statement is read as 'not finite' meaning N infinite (Infinite N), with the answer expected as answer(True) for a positive answer.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition (∀ f.g. G, prime p, minimal normal N that is abelian of exponent p: Finite N ∨ ∀ finite generating S, ∃ c>1, eventually c^n ≤ #(N ∩ CayleyBall S n)); differences are stylistic. c07 is the most idiomatic: Mathlib's `Minimal (fun H => H.Normal ∧ H ≠ ⊥) N` (verified in a scratch file to unfold to: N normal, N ≠ ⊥, every nontrivial normal M ≤ N equals N), `IsMulCommutative N`, `Finite N`, explicit `[Group.FG G]`, and a thorough docstring. Only light docstring/layout edits were made (open moved inside namespace, module docstring expanded). c02 was passed over because its two bespoke definitions and extra API lemma add complexity without gain; c06 drops `Group.FG` (equivalent but less transparent); c04 spells out commutativity by hand.

The single-slot decomposition is correct: the problem is one yes/no question, and the notes' reading (growth function = n ↦ #{x ∈ N : |x|_S ≤ n}; exponential lower bound = ∃ c > 1 with f(n) ≥ c^n for all sufficiently large n; independence from S; positive answer = answer(True)) matches my understanding and what was formalized.

/-!
# Conjecture 7.49

by V. I. Trofimov

namespace Kourovka.«7.49»

open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth

/--
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group, and $N$ a minimal normal subgroup of $G$ which is an
elementary abelian $p$-group. Is it true that either $N$ is finite or the growth function for
the elements of $N$ with respect to a finite generating set of $G$ is bounded below by an
exponential function?

Here $N$ is a minimal normal subgroup of $G$ if it is minimal among the nontrivial normal
subgroups of $G$, and $N$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group ($p$ a prime) if it is abelian and
$x^p = 1$ for all $x \in N$. The growth function for the elements of $N$ with respect to a
finite generating set $S$ of $G$ is $n \mapsto \#\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\}$, where $|x|_S$ is
the word length of $x$ with respect to $S$; the set $\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\}$ is the
intersection of $N$ with the ball of radius $n$ in the Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $S$
(`CayleyBall S n`). It is bounded below by an exponential function if there is a constant
$c > 1$ with $\#\{x \in N : |x|_S \le n\} \ge c^n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This
property does not depend on the choice of the finite generating set $S$ of $G$, so it is
required for every finite generating set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.49» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G] (p : ℕ), p.Prime →
      ∀ N : Subgroup G, Minimal (fun H : Subgroup G => H.Normal ∧ H ≠ ⊥) N →
        IsMulCommutative N → (∀ x ∈ N, x ^ p = 1) →
        Finite N ∨ ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ →
          ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧
            ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (((N : Set G) ∩ CayleyBall S n).ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.49»

items: 'Minimal normal subgroup' is encoded with Mathlib's `Minimal (fun H : Subgroup G => H.Normal ∧ H ≠ ⊥) N`, which unfolds definitionally (verified with Iff.rfl) to: N is normal, N ≠ ⊥, and every nontrivial normal M ≤ N satisfies N ≤ M (i.e. M = N).

'Elementary abelian p-group' is encoded as `p.Prime`, `IsMulCommutative N` (N abelian) and `∀ x ∈ N, x ^ p = 1` (exponent divides p). For p prime this is exactly an F_p-vector space / direct sum of copies of Z/p. The trivial group would satisfy this, but N ≠ ⊥ is forced by minimality.

The growth function for the elements of N is taken inline as n ↦ `((N : Set G) ∩ CayleyBall S n).ncard`, where `GromovPolynomialGrowth.CayleyBall S n` (already in FormalConjecturesForMathlib) is the set of products of ≤ n elements of S ∪ S⁻¹, i.e. the word-length ball. For finite S this set is finite, so `ncard` is the true cardinality (no junk-value issue).

'Bounded below by an exponential function' is encoded as ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c ^ n ≤ growth(n). Since growth(n) ≥ 1 for all n (1 ∈ N ∩ ball), this is equivalent to ∃ c > 1, C > 0, ∀ n, C·c^n ≤ growth(n), and also to liminf growth(n)^{1/n} > 1. Requiring c^n ≤ growth(n) for *all* n was avoided because growth(1) may equal 1 when S ∩ N = ∅.

The finite generating set S is universally quantified (∀ S finite with closure S = ⊤), placed inside the second disjunct as the text does ('either N is finite or the growth function ... w.r.t. a finite generating set ... is bounded below by an exponential'). Exponential lower growth of N is independent of the choice of S (word lengths w.r.t. two finite generating sets are bi-Lipschitz), so ∀ S and ∃ S are equivalent; ∀ S was chosen as the more transparent reading. `[Group.FG G]` is kept as the explicit hypothesis 'G is finitely generated' and guarantees the ∀ S is not vacuous.

'N is finite' is `Finite N` (N coerced to a type), used in the disjunction `Finite N ∨ …`, which is classically equivalent to `Infinite N → …` as suggested in the decomposition notes. answer(True) corresponds to a positive answer to the question.
G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 1_74, 20_76).

reviewer_notes: Checks performed: `GromovPolynomialGrowth.CayleyBall S n` is {products of ≤ n elements of S ∪ S⁻¹}, i.e. the word-length ball, so `(N : Set G) ∩ CayleyBall S n` is exactly {x ∈ N : |x|_S ≤ n}; it is finite for finite S, so `ncard` is the true count. 'Bounded below by an exponential' is taken as ∃ c>1 with f(n) ≥ c^n for all sufficiently large n; this is equivalent to ∃ a>0, c>1, ∀ n, a·c^n ≤ f(n) (since f(n) ≥ 1) and is invariant under change of finite generating set (word metrics are bi-Lipschitz), so quantifying ∀ S is faithful; a 'for all n' bound would be wrongly false when S ∩ N = ∅ (f(1)=1). Elementary abelian p-group encoded as p prime, abelian, x^p = 1 for all x ∈ N; N ≠ ⊥ comes from minimality. answer(True) = positive answer. Relative growth (in G) is the only sensible reading since an infinite elementary abelian N is not itself finitely generated. No candidate omitted the slot.
